review:
A fair warning, this game can probably cause eye strain or epilepsy-related issues. It has some trippy visuals, fast movement, and a bizarre choice where every couple of turns the screen will change to a random color filter. However, if none of that is an issue, this is a cool little indie game worth trying out.

The game itself is really simple, not sure what exactly to classify it as but I guess it's sort of a rhythm game. The only things you do are move left and right, which automatically speeds you up and progresses you further down the path. As you keep moving, a surprisingly neat story is both narrated by a voice and shown through the world changing around you. The main challenge comes from making precise turns as you gain momentum, but sometimes it does also throw an unexpected twist that forces you to make quick decisions. There is also plenty of room to cheese parts of the game through creative parkour or speed control if you really want to. The music is really nice, too, and has unique tracks for each level.

The game will take a few hours at most depending on how quickly you learn the timings. While it does not have any extrinsic replay value, the gameplay lends itself very easily to messing around and trying to break something or beat it more efficiently. If this looks fun to you, it should provide enough to be worth a try.

[h3]A honest review from someone who was very inspired by the game and made my own take on the runner game genre afterwards.[/h3] 
I bought the game twice, first on switch, where I played until level 7 and then on steam where I also played until level 7, but beat that today and is now at level 10, the final one. 



This game is very "artsy" as it is a narrative driven runner game, which is a hard to combine genre, when you cannot stop accelerating and the level goes on, yet this game managed to do it quite well.

[h3]The Story[/h3]
The story itself is about the "simplest office clerk" and you got to deliver a message to the queen of ice. The narrative is told with a computer voice, which speaks the lines after reaching thresholds in the level progression, shown as a % value in the bottom.
The story is neat and a good selling point for the game, if you like a dystopian sounding setting but set in the future but this future are the 90s, but let's be honest the narrative sometimes gets overshadowed if you are concentrated to not fall to your game over. Luckily these messages are short, so the damage is minimal.

[h3]The Gameplay[/h3]
The gameplay is easily explained: run, press left or right, reach 99% and the next level trigger.
The challenge comes from the courses you have to run and the speed you build up, just like the progression %, with your turns. If you turn often, you get faster quickly. You can touch floating cubes, which will most of the time lower your speed and it makes it more manageable.
Also here I have to comment, that the left and right inputs when I played today, where a bit irresponsive sometimes. If you press to quickly you miss your "turn window" and your input gets eaten and you fall probably off the platform.
The gameplay sure is fun, the minimalistic nature makes the path clear and I only dislike when you accelerate into the air and while airborn you cannot see where you are, which lets you guess where you need to land and like I said - you cannot panic-adjust that easily, leaving you more vulnerable that it needs to be.

[h3]The Level[/h3]
All levels have a neat atmosphere but many people, me included, dislike level 7 for its very tight passages at way to high speed. I managed after 2 hours probably in total to beat that level if you count every try on both versions I played. 
Another level I dislike is level 8, because of the use of physic based explosions for some tiles, which will land on the running track and will hinder your vision, so bad that you miss the track completely with the intended way being that you lowered your speed enough beforehand, which is a bit bad, due to you adjusting at some points to much and now you are locked in being too fast and ending up having to guess when a building explodes on top of you.
My last dislike is the final level and its use of platforms with huge gaps in between, which are not a problem with enough speed, but with a problematic possibility, to get stuck in some gaps and you now have to turn and fall in hope for a saving platforms. 
On the other hand though: the final level might be my favourite after all, also because you can save yourself most of the time with how the level is structured,

[h3]The Looks[/h3]
The game has gorgeous 2D sprites throughout every level and I love it. The 3D parts are very simple to say the least, but they are the most clear way to tell the path, they are practical and it does its job, which is appreciated. 
There are glitch effects on the screen, which some are more hindering than others. The inconsistency is annoying honestly and the effects also cause uncomfort for some people, which needs to be considered.

After all though...
I love the game.

I've been seriously obsessed with this game for years. Every few months I pick it up again and go through an intense phase of binging it every chance I get. I own it on Android and iOS as well. Probably you won't play it as much as I have, but who can say?If you like vaporwave visuals, trance electronic music, story-based games, runners, interesting game physics, repetitive gameplay you can really sink into (or all of the above), this game is for you. I'm fond of all of these things. NO THING has some seriously interesting maps that always surprise when you move from one area to another. The soundtrack is fantastic and really gets my pulse racing in specific areas. The robotic narration is really unique, quite poetic, and multifaceted. The fact that you will die and fail and have to hear much of it again is part of the appeal for me and really cements the game's atmosphere.The controls are simple: just pushing left or right to turn. But within that there's actually a lot of subtlety that goes into playing the game. You have to get used to game physics and making turns when it feels like you shouldn't in order to make a landing or take a different route. There's a /ton/ of timing involved, as well. There are certain areas of this game that almost feel like a rhythm game to me, and that's a really impressive crossover of gameplay and soundtrack that's worth recognition. Throughout each level, the speed gradually increases, putting on the pressure. Certain glitch effects and items throughout areas change your perception and can make things easier or harder without much predictability. I find that super fun.This game is somewhat of a stress relief activity for me. If runner games or rhythm games have that effect on you, you'll probably love this game. Honestly, I'd recommend it to anyone who's interested in the trailer. It's worth the buy. I love this game.

I absolutely despised NO THING after my first couple of attempts. It was frustratingly demanding, the graphics didn't seem to add anything to the exasperating mechanics, and the soundtrack seemed to be just a frustrating set of blips and bleeps. But then I beat the first level, and the game suddenly clicked for me. I still felt frustrated and annoyed, but suddenly the game's story had me hooked. 

NO THING, for those who are unaware (and fair enough, the game doesn't really explain itself) is a 1993 dystopic retro-futuristic "semi-infinite" runner game. It knows how runner games work, and it deconstructs the genre through the lens of something that feels like it should be distinctly unfun. It is punishing. You have to follow a track along, growing faster and faster as the level goes on as you try to fill your percentage to 100%. But every time I died, I felt a strange compulsion to keep going. I was going to prove myself against this game. 

So it's definitely not for everyone. It's very, very weird and surreal, and the gameplay is super frustrating. Even in spite of how addicting the actual gameplay is (because damn does it feel rewarding to beat a level), I can't help but wish that there was a "story mode" to play through the game for the story, with a less punishing speed for the protagonist. Still, it's a great stylistic and artistic experiment, and it tells a story in a disjointed, strangely appealing way. Definitely if it's on sale, pick it up and try it, just to see if, on the off chance, it hooks you too.

This is the only endless runner game I've ever played. Something about the art and the audio of this game just caught me completely (and [i]really[/i] stood out where I first picked it up on the Switch.) I can't really explain it. I had the same feeling with Thumper. Ordinarily games in genres I don't much care for, but sometimes you just see a game that looks and sounds like something right up your street and NO THING is right up my street.

NO THING has only 10 levels. The only controls are a turn-left command and a turn-right command. And it's probably some of the most fun I've had playing a game all year. With each turn you make, the game gradually quickens, making the task of getting to the end of the level harder. I've yet to reach beyond level 5, yet to say all I am doing is turning left and right, there has been a good amount of variation. Some levels are circuits, some are point A to point B and there's at least one level with a surpising amount of verticality.

The music is different on each level, but cleaves to the same aesthethic. I can't say I've decoded much of the spoken-story but I cannot begin to imagine this game without that voice ringing out periodically. What I enjoy most of all however is the 'just-one-more-go' quality. Deaths can come quickly, but in a second you can get back into the game and try again. It's challenging, but not punishing. Great in snatched, small doses. And every time you fail you catch yourself thinking 'Again! This time I'll do better!'

I took a chance on something a little different with this and I'm really glad I did. So much so, that I double-dipped. I wish all the punts I took on games went like this!

警告：
1，预告片为实际游戏体验，如果对预告片的光影效果感到不适的人请远离此游戏！
2，对于手残和反应慢的玩家来来说这款游戏极不友好！很有可能你连第一关都过不了！

一款魔性的游戏，操作简单（只需要左右2个键）但是难度高得出奇，我在死了186次后终于通关了，相比于其他人花了5-10个小时通关的人来说，3小时已经是非常快的了。最后2个成就太反人类了，直接放弃。

整个游戏剧情比较无厘头，玩家扮演的是一个普普通通的办公室职员，某天被授予了为冰雪皇后传递消息的任务，需要开车闯过10个关卡到达皇后的城堡，途中会有个机械的声音在给你普及游戏的世界观。

游戏过程就是玩家通过左右进行转弯确保自己不要掉落到悬崖下面去，但是整个画面会不时地改变颜色，调整背景模型甚至出现各种幻觉特效来分散玩家的注意力，同时玩家的速度会逐步提升，稍微一不注意就会车毁人亡然后重新开始这一关。每一关的进度不短，所以请做好无数次死亡的准备，记住这个游戏没有存档点，除了每过一关后会自动存盘以外，你死了即便进程是99%都得重来！

掌握以下窍门会稍微帮助你：
1，玩家车辆行驶的速度并不是随时间而提高，而是你每转一次弯就会略微提升一点点（初始速度是1.5，达到3之前每转一次弯会增加0.05左右，速度过3以后每转一次会增加0.01）。转弯会有一定的延迟。速度3以后的转弯必须要提前不然车很容易冲出道路。
2，前八关出现的红色方块吃了以后会略微减少行车的速度。一些绕圈圈的重复关卡需要好好计算吃方块的时间。第八关以后会出现加速方块，除了第九关需要用到那玩意飞过桥其他任何时候都尽量避免。
3，一部分关卡是单一道路，直接沿着路线走达到目的地就行了，另外一部分关卡设计了绕圈子，需要在一个赛道里面多转几次找到出路才能过关。比较特殊的关卡是第四关，利用好飞车技巧可以少绕一些弯道。
4，第七关是劝退关，是第一关的加强版，将原道路变得更窄，减速的方块会更少，而且要绕4圈才能算过关，请做好无数次翻车的心理准备。
5，最后一关目的地城堡入口需要在最高一层绕1到2圈达到99%才会出现。
